_what_this_is: Migration drift already present when this gate was written, 11 Aug 2026. These are DEBT: each number may fall and may never rise. Lowering one is free and always welcome. Raising one is a decision for the owner, not an edit to this file.
_not_written_by_bless: Set by hand, deliberately. --bless was run and rejected: at the moment of writing another agent had staged the deletion of 20260811063750_baseline_live_schema.sql and left its replacement 20260811160031 untracked, so the tree momentarily contained no baseline dump and --bless would have recorded 588 missing. Blessing a transient is how a ratchet becomes a rubber stamp. The 0 below is the measured count once the on-disk dump is committed, verified by running the comparator against the full on-disk file set: 587 covered by the squash, 0 missing.
_why_duplicates_is_3_and_not_0: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations is an append-only history of what was actually run. These three names each ran twice and that is now a permanent fact; removing the rows would falsify the record of what production executed. The number can only fall if Supabase's own history is ever rebuilt. A FOURTH duplicate fails the build, which is the point: it means apply_migration retried again, and the next retry may land on SQL that is not idempotent.
_why_missing_is_0_and_must_stay_there: There is no historical debt to grandfather here. Every migration applied before the newest baseline dump is genuinely in the repository, because a squash dump IS the source for everything it covers. So the honest limit is zero, and the very next apply_migration that does not write a file takes it to 1 and fails on the spot. That is the hole this gate was built to close.
